saints.name: St. Vincent Ferrer
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: The Dominican “Angel of the Judgment,” whose preaching of penance stirred all of Western Europe…
biography: Born at Valencia on 23 January 1350, Vincent entered the Order of Preachers at eighteen and was ordained priest at Barcelona in 1379; after teaching theology at Lleida he gave himself wholly to preaching. For some twenty years he journeyed through Spain, France, Switzerland, and Italy, drawing vast crowds by his sermons on sin, death, and judgment, whence men called him the Angel of the Judgment.

He lived through the Western Schism and long upheld the Avignon claimant Benedict XIII, whom he served as apostolic penitentiary; but when Benedict refused every path of reunion, Vincent publicly withdrew his obedience, helping to open the way to the settlement reached at the Council of Constance. Multitudes of sinners, and many Jews and Muslims, were reconciled to the Church by his preaching.

Worn out by travel, he died at Vannes in Brittany on 5 April 1419 and was canonized by Callixtus III in 1455. He is honoured as a patron of builders, for he spent his life building up the Church and mending its broken unity.
saints.knownFor: His preaching of repentance and his part in healing the Western Schism.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 5 April
